encodingRules.applies: PIC 9(n) - unsigned zoned decimal, USAGE DISPLAY
encodingRules.decode: n digit characters (EBCDIC X'F0'-X'F9'; in the fixture files the characters 0-9). Anything else rejects the record.

encodingRules.applies: PIC S9(n)V99 - signed zoned decimal, sign in the last byte (trailing overpunch, no SIGN SEPARATE)
encodingRules.decode: last byte carries digit and sign: X'C0'-X'C9' ({ A-I) positive, X'D0'-X'D9' (} J-R) negative, X'F0'-X'F9' accepted as positive; V is an implied decimal point, two places
encodingRules.encode: always C for zero or positive and D for negative (what the golden files hold). An F-signed source digit therefore comes back as C (G02); minus zero comes back as plus zero (G03)

encodingRules.decode: host: EBCDIC code page to be confirmed (G01), fixtures: ISO-8859-1. Stored as CHAR(n), so trailing spaces are kept by padding and ignored in comparisons, as in COBOL. A byte that is not a character of the code page (for example X'00') rejects the record (G07)
encodingRules.encode: padded with spaces to n bytes in the output code page

encodingRules.decode: kept as the n raw bytes in a BYTEA column, no translation
encodingRules.encode: written back byte for byte; for a new interest transaction the filler is n spaces in the output code page (G05)

encodingRules.decode: none of the 43 fields of the five copybooks is COMP-3 or COMP; every field is USAGE DISPLAY. The only binary item the program sees is PARM-LENGTH S9(04) COMP in its LINKAGE SECTION, which is not on any dataset
encodingRules.encode: not needed. The codec must refuse a copybook field whose USAGE is not DISPLAY instead of guessing

encodingRules.decode: VSAM returns TCATBALF in the byte order of the EBCDIC key. The target reads ORDER BY trancat_acct_id, trancat_type_cd COLLATE "C", trancat_cd
encodingRules.encode: equal for all-digit or all-letter type codes; differs when letters and digits are mixed, because EBCDIC sorts letters before digits (G06)

gaps.title: Host code page is not stated
gaps.detail: No CCSID is in the JCL, the copybooks or the scheduler export. The parity tool assumes cp037 for EBCDIC. Needed to decode every PIC X field and the brace and letter sign bytes.
gaps.closes: a statement of the CCSID, or a hex dump of one record per file

gaps.title: Sign of positive zoned numbers on the host
gaps.detail: The golden files hold C-signed positives. Host data written by other programs or loaded by IDCAMS may hold F-signed (unsigned) digits. The value is the same, the byte is not, so a re-encoded record can differ by one byte per amount.
gaps.closes: the compile options (NUMPROC) and a sample of production records

gaps.title: Minus zero
gaps.detail: A zoned field can hold -0 (X'D0' in the last byte). NUMERIC has no minus zero; it is written back as +0.

gaps.title: Dates kept as text
gaps.detail: ACCT-OPEN-DATE, ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE and ACCT-REISSUE-DATE are PIC X(10). The fixtures hold YYYY-MM-DD, but nothing in the stream reads them, so their content on the host is unverified. They stay CHAR(10) so that no record is rejected or changed.
gaps.closes: trial-load profile of the three fields; then a decision whether to type them as DATE

gaps.title: Bytes the program never sets in an interest transaction
gaps.detail: TRAN-DESC is filled by STRING, which does not pad, and the 20-byte FILLER is never moved to. Off-host both hold spaces. On the host they hold whatever working storage held at program start (INT-T04). The target writes spaces.
gaps.closes: one SYSTRAN generation from the host in hex

gaps.title: Key order of mixed type codes
gaps.detail: EBCDIC sorts letters before digits, the C collation sorts digits before letters. If one account has type codes of both kinds, the target reads its balances in a different order and the six-digit transaction counter is handed out differently.
gaps.closes: trial-load profile: distinct TRANCAT-TYPE-CD values (fixtures: digits only)

gaps.title: Text fields with bytes that are not characters
gaps.detail: A PIC X field holding low-values or packed data cannot be stored in CHAR. The loader rejects the record and the trial load fails; it does not substitute a character.
gaps.closes: trial-load reject count (expected 0) or a rule per field

gaps.title: Accounts with more than one card
gaps.detail: The alternate index on XREF-ACCT-ID is not unique. Which record CBACT04C gets, or whether it stops with status 02, is not determined by the source (INT-H03). The target stops the run (policy switch multiCard = STOP) until the register row is answered.
gaps.closes: INT-H03 answered; trial-load profile: number of accounts with several cards

gaps.title: Category code is numeric here and CHAR(4) in the Db2 tables
gaps.detail: TRANCAT-CD, DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD and TRAN-CAT-CD are PIC 9(04) and map to NUMERIC(4,0). carddemo.transaction_type_categor.trc_type_category is CHAR(4) (db/postgres/01-transaction-type.sql). No foreign key is defined between them; the legacy files have none either.
gaps.closes: a decision on one type for the category code across the schema

gaps.title: Timestamps kept as text
gaps.detail: TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are PIC X(26) in the form YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000, which is not a PostgreSQL timestamp literal. They stay CHAR(26) so the exported record is exact.
gaps.closes: a decision when the transaction history itself moves

gaps.title: Volumes are unknown
gaps.detail: The estate holds no record counts for the production files. Chunk size, load time and whether the whole job fits the window between CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL cannot be sized.
gaps.closes: LISTCAT record counts of the four input files and the run time of INTCALC

gaps.title: Which DD serves the read by account id
gaps.detail: CBACT04C reads XREF-FILE by its alternate key but never names DD XREFFIL1; the edge is a candidate (manifest D3, ask A5). The target reads card_xref through card_xref_acct_ix either way.

buildSteps.title: Schema for the interest stream

buildSteps.title: Record codec for the five copybooks
buildSteps.outcome: A copybook-driven codec decodes and encodes every field of the five layouts in the fixture code page and in EBCDIC, byte for byte.

buildSteps.title: Complete calculation rules behind the policy switches
buildSteps.outcome: The calculation covers every rule and every as-coded quirk of the rulebook, and all seven fixture cases pass through the file adapters.

buildSteps.title: Loader for the four unloaded files with reconciliation figures
buildSteps.outcome: loadExtractsStep replaces the four replica tables from the unloaded files and records the counts and sums the strategy asks for.

buildSteps.title: Calculation step on PostgreSQL with commit and restart boundaries
buildSteps.outcome: calcInterestStep reads the replica tables, writes interest_transaction and updates account, one account per item, and a failed run can be restarted without charging twice.

buildSteps.title: Export of SYSTRAN, the ACCTDATA image and return codes
buildSteps.outcome: exportDatasetsStep writes a run's results from the tables in the recorded fixture format and as fixed-length host files.

buildSteps.title: Error paths and stop conditions
buildSteps.outcome: Every condition under which CBACT04C abends, and the two holes the source does not determine, stop the new job in a defined, tested way.

buildSteps.title: Gate: seven-case parity through the database, in CI
buildSteps.outcome: make parity-java runs load, calculation and export through PostgreSQL for all seven cases, passes the comparator, and is a required CI check.

buildSteps.title: Gate: reconciliation report and side-by-side comparison kit
buildSteps.outcome: One command produces the reconciliation report of a load and a run, and one compares a legacy run's files with a target run's files, so the trial load and the side-by-side period can be executed.

dataMoves.title: Trial load
dataMoves.intro: Copy the four input files into PostgreSQL once, outside any production run, to find data the mapping cannot hold.

dataMoves.title: Reconciliation counts and sums
dataMoves.intro: Figures that must be equal on both sides. Each is computed by the loader or the exporter and stored in interest_run.

dataMoves.title: Side-by-side running
dataMoves.intro: Both jobs process the same inputs; only the mainframe result is used.

dataMoves.title: Cutover
dataMoves.intro: The cycle in which the new job's result is the one that is used.

dataMoves.title: Fallback
dataMoves.intro: What happens if the cutover run is not accepted, by the point reached.

dataItems.text: Unload TCATBALF, DISCGRP, CARDXREF and ACCTDATA to flat files with IDCAMS REPRO while the CICS files are closed, so the four files are from the same moment.
Transfer the files in binary with their record length (50, 50, 50, 300); no character translation on the way.
Load each file into its empty table in one transaction. A record that cannot be decoded goes to a reject list with file, record number and field; one reject fails the trial.

Profile what the mapping gaps ask for: accounts with several cards (G08), mixed type codes (G06), minus zero (G03), F-signed amounts (G02), fillers that are not blank, accounts that are not active (INT-H04), balances without a rate and without a DEFAULT rate (INT-R08).
Run the trial on data approved for the environment; this repository holds synthetic data only.
Row count of each of the four tables equals the record count of its unloaded file.

Sums equal on both sides: ACCT-CURR-BAL, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT over accounts; TRAN-CAT-BAL over balances; DIS-INT-RATE over rates; and the sum of the account ids of each file as a hash total.
Round trip: every loaded row, encoded again, equals its source record byte for byte. Differences are counted per gap id (G02, G03); any other difference fails.
Keys: the number of distinct keys equals the row count in each table, and the lowest and highest key equal the first and last record of the file.

After the calculation: the number of rows written to interest_transaction equals the records in the exported SYSTRAN generation, and the sum of TRAN-AMT equals the change of the sum of ACCT-CURR-BAL plus the interest of the last account (which is not added, INT-Q04).
After the write-back: ACCTDATA unloaded again equals the account table in count and in the five sums of RC2.
Off-host first: make parity-java passes the seven fixture cases field by field (ticket 09).

Shadow run per cycle: unload the inputs just before INTCALC, let INTCALC run as today, run the new job on the unload, and compare SYSTRAN, the ACCTDATA after-image and SYSOUT with the field-level comparator. The new job's output is not given to COMBTRAN.

Timestamps: the two runs happen at different moments (INT-Q03), so TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are compared for format only, or the new job is given the mainframe run's clock. The rule used is written into the comparison report.
Every difference is classified as a defect, an open decision (its id) or a mapping gap (its id). Exit needs REL-04 cycles with no defect and no unclassified difference.
The number of cycles and the bar for 'equal' are release decisions REL-04 and REL-05.
Preconditions: tickets 09 and 10 are closed, REL-01 to REL-13 are answered, and each row of the decision register is answered or accepted as coded.

Order inside the window: CLOSEFIL, back up ACCTDATA, unload the four files, load and reconcile (RC1-RC4), calculate, export, reconcile (RC5), write back ACCTDATA and catalog the SYSTRAN generation, reconcile (RC6), COMBTRAN, WAITSTEP, OPENFIL.
Scheduler: the INTCALC definition in the folder is replaced by the job that starts the new run; it still adds the condition MONTHLY-InterestCalculation-INTCALC, so COMBTRAN is released as before.
Go or no-go is taken after RC5 and before the write-back. Until then nothing on the mainframe has changed.
The legacy job and load module stay in place, unscheduled, for the period agreed in REL-13.
Before the write-back: abandon the new run and run the legacy INTCALC in the same window. Nothing on the mainframe needs restoring.
After the write-back and before COMBTRAN: restore ACCTDATA from the backup of CO2, delete the cataloged SYSTRAN generation, run the legacy INTCALC.
After COMBTRAN or OPENFIL: no technical fallback. Corrections are posted as transactions; that is a business decision (REL-07).
FB1 and FB2 are rehearsed once during the side-by-side period.
On the PostgreSQL side the run is marked ABANDONED in interest_run; the replica tables are replaced by the next load.

registerDecisions.question: Should monthly interest be cut off at the cent, or rounded?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - truncate towards zero

registerDecisions.question: Where should the date part of the interest transaction id come from?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - the PARM literal of the job, changed by hand or by the scheduler for each run

registerDecisions.question: Which date and time should an interest transaction carry?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - the system clock of the run

registerDecisions.question: Should the last account on the file have its interest added to its balance like every other account?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - the last account is not updated
registerDecisions.where: interest-calc, account break at end of input

registerDecisions.question: Should a credit balance be paid interest at the lending rate?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - negative interest is posted

registerDecisions.question: Should a zero-amount interest transaction be written?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Keep as coded - write the 0.00 transaction

registerDecisions.question: Are fees charged anywhere else, or is a fee rule missing from this job?
registerDecisions.asCoded: No fees in this job (as coded)
registerDecisions.where: interest-calc, after the interest of a balance

registerDecisions.question: What stops a second run in the same cycle, and how is a failed run restarted?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Operations procedure only (as the estate shows) - restore the account file and rerun from the start

registerDecisions.question: Which card number belongs on the interest transaction of an account with several cards?
registerDecisions.default: STOP (proposed - the source does not determine it)

registerDecisions.question: Should an inactive account still be charged interest on its balances?
registerDecisions.asCoded: Yes - charge every account with a balance (as coded)

registerDecisions.question: Are these limits acceptable, and what should happen if one is reached?
registerDecisions.default: STOP (proposed - the source does not determine it)

registerDecisions.question: In which order do posting, the file reloads and the interest run happen, and on which day of the month?
registerDecisions.default: the order of the Control-M folder as exported

releaseDecisions.question: How does the new job share data with the jobs that stay on the mainframe?
options: A file bridge at the dataset boundary: unload, load, run, export, write back (proposed)
B replicate the VSAM files continuously into PostgreSQL
C move every reader and writer of the four files first

releaseDecisions.question: Which copy of the account data is the system of record while POSTTRAN and the CICS programs stay?
options: A the mainframe file ACCTDATA; the PostgreSQL table is a copy refreshed for each run (proposed)
B the PostgreSQL table

releaseDecisions.question: What is written back to ACCTDATA after a run?
options: A the whole record of every account the run updated, while the CICS files are closed (proposed)
B the whole file

releaseDecisions.question: How many cycles run side by side before cutover?
options: A two consecutive cycles with no unexplained difference (proposed)
B another number

releaseDecisions.question: What is the bar for 'equal' in the side-by-side run?
options: A every field of every record of SYSTRAN and ACCTDATA equal, timestamps compared under the rule of SS3 (proposed)
B totals only

releaseDecisions.question: In which cycle does the new job take over?
options: A the first cycle after REL-04 is met and every gate is green (proposed)
B a fixed date

releaseDecisions.question: Until which point can a cutover run be abandoned without a business correction?
options: A until COMBTRAN starts; after that only a forward fix (proposed)
B another point

releaseDecisions.question: Which code page and sign convention do the unloaded files use?
options: A as the parity tool assumes: cp037, C/D signs (proposed, unconfirmed)
B other, stated by the data owner

releaseDecisions.question: Who starts the new job?
options: A the existing Control-M folder; the INTCALC job definition is replaced and keeps its condition names (proposed)
B a new scheduler

releaseDecisions.question: What does a failed run report to the scheduler?
options: A a non-zero exit code mapped to NOTOK, with the legacy message text in the log (proposed)
B a specific code agreed with operations in place of user abend 999

releaseDecisions.question: How is a run that failed part-way continued?
options: A restart of the same run from the last committed account (proposed; the legacy procedure is INT-H02)
B restore and rerun from the start, as on the mainframe

releaseDecisions.question: How long are a run's rows kept in interest_transaction and interest_run?
options: A five runs, as GDG LIMIT(5) keeps five generations (proposed)
B another retention

releaseDecisions.question: How long does the legacy INTCALC job stay available as a fallback after cutover?
options: A two cycles after the cutover cycle (proposed)
B another period
